annotation.reasoning_summary: Polygons represent discrete housing association property footprints/projects rather than a full tessellation or reporting unit. The decisive rule is object: identifiable real-world bounded assets with numeric attributes about dwelling counts.
Point features mark individual archaeological cesspits/finds at addresses, so this is a set of distinct objects rather than measurements or events.
Point features mark distinct archaeological finds/locations (water soil objects) with object codes and photos, so this is a point object layer, not a measurement or event layer.

Polygon features mark discrete archaeological sites/vindplaatsen with names, addresses, and descriptions; they are bounded objects/locations rather than a full tessellation, coverage, or amount layer.

Polygon regions mark selected parks/areas with BBQ restrictions; they are bounded phenomenon zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units. Entity is PatchDS because the layer maps restricted barbecue areas/permissions, not objects or amounts.

Polygon areas are discrete protected city/district/village heritage zones, not a full tessellation. The decisive rule is object: each region represents a named conservation area with status and designation date.

Point features mark observation locations for wild bees at named places and years. This is a point object layer, not a measurement or amount layer; the decisive rule is ObjectDS for countable observed occurrences.
Point layer for honey bee locations; the main mapped phenomenon is the numeric quantity of colonies/hives at each point, so PointDS + AmountDS.

Polygon regions represent soil-quality zones and classifications across the area rather than a reporting-unit tessellation; the decisive rule is full-area thematic coverage (soil quality / bodemfunctie classes), so CoverageDS.
Point features represent individual trees with identifiers, species, and attributes; this is an object layer, not a measurement or amount layer.
Point geometry with 70k features representing individual trees (named species, tree number, owner/manager, plant year); this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features represent individual trees (countable real-world objects). Numeric fields like boomnummer, height, and plant year are attributes, not the main mapped phenomenon.

Point layer of individual trees; each point represents a distinct real-world object, not a measurement or event. Numeric fields like Boomnummer, Plantjaar, and RADIUS are attributes, so ObjectDS applies.
Point features mark discrete neighborhood compost locations/initiatives (street name, initiator, start year). This is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Polygon areas named as camera zones; they are selected bounded areas rather than a full tessellation, so geometry is PlainVectorRegion and entity is PatchDS.
Point features represent individual trees (Canadian poplars) with object attributes like species, district, and maintenance/planning actions; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event map.
Point layer of crowd-monitoring sensors/cameras; each feature is a distinct facility/object, not a measurement or event. Numeric fields like rotation are just attributes.

Polygons mark named cultural-historical study areas / project sites rather than a full tessellation or reporting units, so Geometry is PlainVectorRegion. The regions represent identifiable bounded places/areas with descriptions and study metadata, best treated as ObjectDS.
Point features mark knotweed occurrences/locations, with species type and photos as attributes; this is an object layer rather than a measurement or event layer.
Point features mark individual ecopassage problem/solution locations (barriers and planned measures) rather than measurements or events; classify as points representing discrete objects.

Polygon/MultiPolygon areas are discrete potential wind-energy sites, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is patch: selected bounded areas with numeric capacity/output attributes, where the regions themselves are the mapped features.

Point locations are polling stations/stemlocaties, but the layer’s main message is election vote totals and percentages per location. Classified as point-based amount mapping rather than object or event.
Point features mark individual trees with oak processionary caterpillar nests/status; this is a point object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Polygon areas marking where pedicabs are allowed/forbidden at certain times; these are selected regulatory zones, not a full tessellation or object layer, so PatchDS with PlainVectorRegion.
Point features denote pedicab pitch locations (standplaatsen), which are distinct real-world facilities/places rather than measurements or events.
Point features represent discrete non-residential buildings/addresses with function labels and IDs; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.

Polygon layer forms a near-complete tessellation of Amsterdam blocks/streets, and the main phenomenon is full-area functional classification (WON/VZN/WRK mix) rather than individual objects or reporting units.

Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, so this is a tessellation. The features are statistical/reporting units (buurtcombinaties) with area attributes, which fits LatticeDS.
Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam (tessellation), and they are reporting/statistical units with area attributes, so LatticeDS.
Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, so geometry is a tessellation. They are reporting/administrative units (buurten) with codes and area, so entity is LatticeDS.
Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, so the geometry is a tessellation and the feature type is a reporting/statistical unit (buurten), not an object or amount map.
City districts are administrative reporting units forming a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, so this is a tessellation and the decisive entity rule is reporting unit/lattice.
City districts are administrative reporting units that partition Amsterdam; the polygon layer forms a near-complete tessellation, so Geometry is VectorTessellation and Entity is LatticeDS.

Polygon areas named as Amsterdam areas and stadsdeel-linked reporting units form a near-complete area partition, so this is a tessellation with lattice/reporting-unit meaning; Opp_m2 is just an attribute.
Municipal area polygons that partition Amsterdam into 22 areas; this is a reporting/administrative tessellation, and Opp_m2 is just an attribute of those units.

Polygon regions are discrete named practice areas, not a full tessellation or reporting lattice. The decisive rule is object: each area is a bounded real-world administrative/managed area with an area attribute, so ObjectDS fits better than AmountDS.

These are practice-area polygons intended as a complete area division of Amsterdam, so the geometry is a tessellation. They function as reporting/administrative units with names and area attributes, so the entity is LatticeDS.
Polygon/MultiPolygon features are discrete contour zones for industrial noise levels (e.g. 50DB), so this is a contour-style region layer rather than a tessellation or object layer.
Polygon zones represent noise contour bands (55-60 dB, 60-65 dB, etc.), so this is a contour/interval layer rather than a tessellation or object map.
Polygon areas represent noise contour bands (50-55 dB, etc.), so this is a contour/interval map rather than a tessellation or object layer.
Polygon noise contour bands with dB classes indicate isoline/interval zones rather than a tessellation or reporting units; decisive rule is contour classification.
Point layer of election polling locations/stembureaus; each point is a distinct facility/object, while vote counts and percentages are attributes rather than the mapped phenomenon.
Point features mark discrete green roof locations/projects. The numeric fields are attributes (area, year) rather than the main mapped phenomenon, so this is an object layer, not AmountDS.
Polygon layer of land use classes forming an area-wide categorical coverage; decisive rules are tessellation for geometry and full-area thematic classification for CoverageDS.
Point geometry with named historical buildings/structures; the decisive rule is object, not amount. The year fields are attributes of the buildings, so this is ObjectDS.

The layer shows a few municipality-shaped polygons that are not a full tessellation; the title suggests a size comparison for Amsterdam-related bounded areas, and the decisive rule is object-like regions rather than reporting units, coverage, or amount mapping.
Polygon areas mark selected dog off-leash and ban zones, not a full tessellation or reporting unit; this fits bounded phenomenon patches.

Polygon layer of named green-structure sites and areas (parks, corridors, cemeteries, etc.); these are discrete bounded objects/managed areas, not a reporting tessellation or full-area coverage. Numeric area fields are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point features represent individual elm trees (private). The layer is an inventory of distinct objects with species and attributes, not a measurement or event layer.

Point features represent identifiable housing projects/buildings for youth and students; the numeric dwelling count is an attribute, not the main mapped phenomenon. ObjectDS fits better than AmountDS.
Point features represent individual chestnut trees/records with species and damage status; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point layer with sampled groundwater/drought-related numeric values at locations; decisive rule is point measurements of a continuous phenomenon rather than point objects or amounts.
Polygons are discrete flood zones/interval classes rather than a full tessellation. The layer maps flood chance and depth bands, so the decisive rule is contour-like value classes.
Point layer of named markets/market locations; each feature is a distinct real-world place, so ObjectDS with point geometry.
Point features represent named green monuments/park sites with identifiers and status; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features represent identifiable monumental trees (distinct real-world objects); numeric fields are just attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point features represent individual monuments/buildings and related heritage objects; numeric Monumentnummer is just an identifier, so this is ObjectDS on point geometry.

Point features mark individual quay wall plant occurrences/species locations; the layer is about identifiable biological objects at points, not measurements or events. Numeric count fields are attributes, but the main phenomenon is the mapped plant objects.
Polygons form reporting units/tessellated areas with NO2 numeric values by year and 4-week periods, so the decisive rules are tessellation + amount.
Point locations of NO2 measurement sites; the layer is about sampled pollutant measurements at points, so PointDS with PointMeasuresDS. Decisive rule: point measurement layer.
Polygon areas represent selected gulch zones rather than a full tessellation; the categorical field is secondary. Best fit is a bounded phenomenon patch, not coverage or reporting units.
Point soundings/boreholes measuring subsurface values at locations; decisive rule is point measurement sampling of a continuous phenomenon.

Polygon layer of named development neighbourhoods; these are discrete bounded places/managed areas, not a full tessellation or reporting-unit statistics. Entity classified as ObjectDS based on identifiable neighbourhood objects.
Point features representing discrete public toilet facilities; numeric price and opening hours are attributes, not the main phenomenon. Classified as object points.
Polygons are neighbourhood-level areas covering Amsterdam and encode a policy classification/selection field (SELECTIE), so this is a tessellated area-wide thematic coverage layer.
Polygons encode parking standard categories (A/B/C) as an area-wide thematic classification, so this is a coverage layer rather than reporting units or patches.
Polygon footprints of named parks/green spaces; they are discrete managed objects rather than a full tessellation. Numeric area is just an attribute, so the decisive rule is object.
Postcode4 areas are reporting/statistical units that partition the city; the decisive rule is reporting-unit tessellation, not the numeric area attribute Opp_m2.
Postcode4 areas are reporting/statistical units that partition the city, so the geometry is a tessellation and the entity is a lattice; Opp_m2 is just an attribute.
Polygon postcode6 areas form a near-complete tessellation of Amsterdam, and they are reporting/statistical units identified by postcode and buurtcode, so LatticeDS.
LineString layer of plus and main transport infrastructure networks; decisive rule is network/system of connected routes rather than individual objects or amounts.

Polygons/MultiPolygons are discrete pedestrian network areas, not a full tessellation. The layer name and category field (park/plein) indicate identifiable bounded objects/zones, so ObjectDS is the best fit.
Point features represent named locations/assets (masts) with privacy links; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features mark discrete privacy-related items/links to specific privacy statements and research types, not measurements or events; classified as point objects.
Point features mark distinct scan locations/addresses for the car fleet scan; this is a set of identifiable objects/places, not measurements or events.
Point layer of polling/stem locations for the 2019 provincial elections; each point is a distinct voting location/object, with election counts as attributes rather than the main mapped phenomenon.
Polygon patches indicating whether drainage is possible or not; not a full tessellation or reporting unit, so PlainVectorRegion + ExistenceDS based on presence/absence.

Polygons are discrete hydro units, not a full tessellation or reporting grid, so Geometry is PlainVectorRegion. The layer marks selected Rainproof intervention/solution areas (hydro units), which fits PatchDS rather than ObjectDS or CoverageDS.
Polygon areas mark specific rainproof bottleneck zones (selected problem areas), not a full tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is PatchDS for bounded phenomenon areas.
Discrete polygon areas named by location for the Rainproof polder sewerage layer; they are bounded project/object areas, not a full tessellation or numeric amount map.
Point features represent religious buildings/facilities at addresses, so this is a point object layer, not amounts or events.
Line geometries represent sidewalk segments along the street system, so this is a network layer; numeric width/obstacle fields are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
LineString features describe roadway segments for moped rerouting/road use; this is a connected transport network, so LineDS + NetworkDS.
Point features represent individual public sports facilities/playgrounds, not measurements or events. Decisive rule: identifiable real-world objects at point locations -> ObjectDS.
Point locations of city farming sites; each point is a distinct real-world place/facility (object), not a measurement or event.
Polygon footprints represent named city-farming sites/parks with descriptive attributes, so this is a set of discrete objects rather than a tessellation or patch. Main rule used: object.

Point layer of identifiable initiatives/facilities with names, activities, sectors, and years; the decisive rule is ObjectDS for distinct real-world objects, not AmountDS because the numeric field is just an attribute.
LineString layer of major streets; the decisive rule is network/route system, not the numeric line number attribute.
LineString features represent a district heating/cooling transport system, so the decisive rule is network infrastructure rather than object or amount.

Polygon areas are discrete district energy zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is bounded phenomenon patches: neighborhood heat/cold network areas with status categories.

Polygons depict discrete housing plan/project areas rather than a full-area tessellation; they are identifiable development objects/projects with attributes like project name and max dwellings, so ObjectDS fits better than AmountDS.
Point features represent distinct local farm-product businesses/markets with names and addresses; the layer is a set of identifiable objects, not a measurement or event layer.
LineString features for tram and metro lines; decisive rule is connected transport route system, so Geometry=LineDS and Entity=NetworkDS.
LineString features representing tram and metro routes; decisive rule is network/route system, not amount or object.
Point features representing distinct transit facilities (tram stops and metro stations); numeric RADIUS is just an attribute, so classify as ObjectDS.
Point features marking tram stops and metro stations; the decisive rule is network infrastructure, even though each point is a station location.
Point layer of individual traffic lights at crossings; the main phenomenon is identifiable objects/facilities, not measurements or events.
Line network of road links with traffic forecast volumes; geometry is LineDS and the mapped phenomenon is numeric flow amount on links, so AmountDS.
Point layer of election polling locations (stemlocaties). The points represent distinct real-world voting stations; vote totals are attributes, so this fits ObjectDS, not AmountDS.
Point features represent individual trees as identifiable real-world objects; numeric fields are attributes (species, planting year, size classes), not the main mapped phenomenon.

Point layer of identifiable traffic information devices (cameras, displays, sensors); classified as ObjectDS rather than AmountDS because points represent facilities/objects with attributes, not a numeric phenomenon.
Point features represent distinct traffic information system installations (BFA devices/pollers) at named standplaatsen, so this is a point object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features mark distinct bird nesting locations/species occurrences; the numeric Aantal fields are attributes of those objects, not the main mapped phenomenon.
Point features represent individual Vondelpark benches, which are discrete real-world objects; numeric fields like rotation are just attributes, not the main phenomenon.

Line geometries represent street segments/straatvakken, which are discrete linear objects rather than a network-wide flow or amount layer. The categorical walkability and crowding fields are attributes of those objects, so ObjectDS fits best.
Point features represent individual wall art objects at specific building addresses, so this is a point-based object layer rather than a measurement or event layer.
Polygon regions represent an area-wide thematic classification of building/urban welstand levels, not reporting units or selected patches; decisive rule: full-area categorical coverage.
Polygon regions classify the whole area into building/urban system categories; this is a full-area thematic coverage rather than reporting units or selected patches.
Point features mark WWII attack incidents/occurrences at addresses, so the decisive classification is event-at-location rather than objects or amounts.
Polygon layer of discrete housing development projects/plans; features are project areas with names and counts, so classify as bounded objects rather than a tessellation or amount map.
Point layer of identifiable self-build plot projects/locations; the numeric fields are attributes, not the main mapped phenomenon, so classify as ObjectDS.
Polygon layer with categorical classes covering heritage/solar-panel suitability across areas; this is best treated as a full-area thematic coverage, not reporting units or discrete objects.
Point features represent solar panel locations/objects, but the layer’s main mapped meaning is numeric magnitude via detected panel count and power. Point Amount check applies, so PointDS + AmountDS.
Point features represent named swimming-water locations/facilities (beaches, pools, play waters) rather than measurements or events, so this is PointDS + ObjectDS.
